Frontend cpu_cores mean 0.180301 (min 0.157986, max 0.199107); checkoutservice cpu_cores mean 0.046915; paymentservice cpu_cores mean 0.011197 with a slightly negative slope_per_second. Memory slope_per_second is positive for all three (checkoutservice 1883.45, frontend 2239.44, paymentservice 4658.28 bytes/s) with positive split_half_shift values (300032, 355328, 610304 bytes). No CPU/memory limits, requests, quotas, idle baselines or pre-run comparisons appear anywhere in the evidence.

Two limits dominate the interpretation. First, the OpenSearch "errors" profile FAILED with reason SOURCE_HTTP_ERROR after 3 requests and 2 retries (throttle_wait_ms 5986), while the Prometheus "metrics-direct" profile was COMPLETE with all six queries SUCCESS; overall source status is PARTIAL. The zero error counts therefore come from client-side JTL samples, and server-side error telemetry is absent rather than confirmed zero. Second, window_policy_summary reports business_verdict PASS, resource_verdict NO_POLICY, verdict PASS, backed by exactly one policy check (error_rate_ratio, operator lte, threshold 0.01, observed 0/36034, status PASS). NO_POLICY means no resource rule was evaluated — it is not a resource pass — and no latency or per-transaction policy check is present. Note also that the policy denominator 36,034 differs from the overall metric-summary sample_count 37,349, and that resource_binding reports clock_alignment "not_verified_by_core" with 1 leading cell (10,309 ms) and 1 trailing cell (4,660 ms) dropped, so the resource view is narrower than the run window and no lead/lag or temporal causal ordering can be supported until clocks are verified. This advisory does not change the verdict.
